sandbox_argv:
This exploration produces ONE mechanism. You are one of three independent reviewers; you see the same frozen evidence bundle and the same proposals as the others, and you do not coordinate with them before handing in.
THE RESEARCH OBJECTIVE:
Discover new mechanisms in which TRAINING-ONLY user behaviour and HYPERBOLIC geometry are computationally coupled to improve the RQ-VAE Semantic IDs used by a generative next-item recommender, with the real target of Stage3 test Recall@10 above 0.065.
THE SCOPE CONTRACT (a proposal that misses it is sent back, not scored):
A proposal is IN SCOPE only when all of this holds:
  1. BEHAVIOUR: it names one training-only behaviour signal (directed item transitions, user-interest branching, sequential co-consumption, popularity-adjusted graph neighbours, behaviour-conditioned assignment weights, ...) and says how it is computed.
  2. HYPERBOLIC GEOMETRY: it names an explicit curved operation (trainable or fixed negative curvature, Poincare or Lorentz distance, exp/log maps, geodesic scoring, curved residual, curved quantization, curved regularization) and where in training or quantization it acts.
  3. REAL COUPLING: one connected computational pathway uses both, so that removing either changes the core computation. A behaviour suffix on an unchanged Euclidean quantizer, a standalone hyperbolic loss beside an unrelated behaviour loss, a geometry name without geometric computation, or inherited unused hyperbolic code do NOT qualify.
  4. TESTABLE EFFECT: it states what should observably change (SID assignment, gradient or parameter update, prefix behaviour predictability, or Stage3 Recall) and names the behaviour-off, geometry-off/Euclidean and both-on comparisons. The three switches must be part of the mechanism, so that the coupling can be shown to be real, but the round RUNS no ablation arm: each candidate is trained once.
  5. MINIMAL SPECIFICATION: equations or pseudocode, inputs and outputs, numerical safeguards and the training cost. No proof and no paper section are required.
SID quality (ER, prefix counts, collisions) is NOT a scope criterion and NOT an admission rule.

EXPERIMENT POLICY (binding on every proposal, implementation and review):
  - ONE candidate, ONE training run, on the frozen budget (3000 Stage 2 epochs on four cards, the frozen Stage 3 protocol, no early stopping).
  - NO ablation experiments: the behaviour-off, geometry-off and both-on switches must EXIST in the code and must be correct, but no arm is trained with them switched off.
  - NO tuning experiments: no sweep over the coupling weight, the clip bound, the temperature, the usage weight or any other constant. A constant that enters the mechanism has to be DERIVED (a scale-relative bound, a measured quantity, a documented default), not chosen by trying values.
  - NO multi-seed experiments: a candidate is not repeated with other seeds, so a single run decides it and the seed noise is part of the uncertainty.
  - The behavioural diagnostics (coherence, adjacency, transfer predictability) are recorded, never used as an admission gate; Stage 3 test_recall@10 is the judgement.
  - A proposal that needs an ablation, a sweep or a seed repetition to make its case is out of programme: it has to make the case with one run.
THE SELECTION POLICY (rank-2026-10-v1): the reviewers RANK the proposals. The proposal the reviewers place best, in total, is the round's mechanism. Rank every proposal, best first, and give each one a reason that names the evidence you used.
Read the frozen evidence bundle for each proposal before you place it: a placement you cannot ground in the evidence is not a placement.
Write PLAIN TEXT, one line per proposal, in exactly this shape:
RANK: <idea_id> | position=<1 for the best, then 2, 3, ...> | reason=<one line>
RANK: <idea_id> | position=<n> | reason=<one line>
Every proposal must appear exactly once, the positions must be 1..N with no ties and no gaps, and the reason must say what in the evidence put the proposal there. If you cannot ground a proposal in the evidence, rank it last and say so in its reason; do not leave a proposal out.
THE PROPOSALS:
IDEA: GYRO-BEHAFF-SID
TITLE: Möbius-gyro residual RQ with behaviour-affinity-weighted Poincaré deep assignment (K = 256/512/512)
MOTIVATION: The measured failure across rounds one and two is depth collapse, not codeword shortage: 24556 training items give 1251 distinct L2 pairs (19.6 items per cell) but only 1298 distinct L3 triples — about 1.04 L3 codes per L2 cell, so the third token carries almost no information. Round one, which kept 1.76 L3 codes per cell, scored 0.0544 against round two's 0.0517. The cause is structural: the third-level tangent residual r^3 = r^2 − log_0(c_2) is near zero for most items, so the ball degenerates to flat space exactly where the finest partition is needed. Every mechanism so far tried to fix depth by moving items (toward a behaviour hub, along a geodesic step) and every one of them merged prefixes.
NOVELTY: Two pieces that are absent from the tried set (poincare-frechet-successor-codebook, CURVCTRL-SID, BRad-RQ, behcone-prefix-rq, succboost-geoshift, LORENTZ-SUCCPROFILE-SMOOTH-RQ, MIXCURV-FIBRE-RQ, BRANCHCURV-MOEB-RQ, TSG-SID). (i) The residual algebra is changed from tangent subtraction to Poincaré gyro-subtraction, with the decoder defined as the Möbius gyro-sum, so the greedy residual is exact by gyro-cancellation and no gain constant is introduced. (ii) The deep-level assignment cost is the Poincaré distance multiplied per (item, codeword) by (1 − a_ik), a train-only successor-profile affinity, so behaviour chooses which of 512 deep codes an item receives. Prior mechanisms moved codebook positions, set per-level curvature, ranked items radially, or applied cones/boosts; none changes the residual algebra, and none makes the distance non-monotone per pair so that behaviour can actually flip the argmin and therefore the token.
CHANGE: Replace the RQ residual subtraction with Poincaré gyro-subtraction and the reconstruction with the Möbius gyro-sum of the chosen codewords, and at levels 2 and 3 multiply each Poincaré distance by (1 − a_ik) before the argmin, with 512 codewords at those levels.
SPECIFICATION: {'text': "Fixed curvature c = 1 (curvature is a gauge; the encoder's tanh scaling absorbs the scale, so no curvature value is chosen or swept). Ball B = {v ∈ R^d : ‖v‖ < 1}. Möbius addition x ⊕ y = ((1 + 2⟨x,y⟩ + ‖y‖²)x + (1 − ‖x‖²)y) / (1 + 2⟨x,y⟩ + ‖x‖²‖y‖²); gyro-subtraction x ⊖ y = x ⊕ (−y). Poincaré distance d_P(x,y) = arcosh(1 + 2‖x−y‖² / ((1−‖x‖²)(1−‖y‖²))). Encoder emits t_i ∈ R^d, v_i = tanh(‖t_i‖/2) · t_i/‖t_i‖. RQ recursion: r^0_i = v_i; for ℓ = 1,2,3, k^ℓ_i = argmin_k [ d_P(r^{ℓ−1}_i, c_{ℓk}) · (1 − γ a^ℓ_{ik}) ] with γ = 1, then r^ℓ_i = r^{ℓ−1}_i ⊖ c_{ℓ,k^ℓ_i}. Reconstruction ẑ_i = c_{1,k¹} ⊕ c_{2,k²} ⊕ c_{3,k³}; loss L = d_P(v_i, ẑ_i)² + β_com·Σ_ℓ ‖log_0(r^ℓ_i)‖² (β_com inherited unchanged from the frozen recipe). Level 1 uses γ_1 = 0 so the coarse semantic hierarchy stays purely geometric; the coupling is confined to levels 2 and 3. a^ℓ_{ik} = max(0, cos(π_i − π̄, π^ℓ_k − π̄)), with π_i a fixed 256-bin successor profile, π̄ its mean, and π^ℓ_k an EMA (decay 0.99) of π_i over items currently assigned to codeword k at level ℓ, stop-gradient. Soft assignment for the straight-through gradient uses softmax(−C^ℓ_{ik}/ε) with ε = median_{i,k} C^ℓ_{ik} over the batch, detached."}
COST: Baseline 0.145–0.16 s per epoch on four GPUs. The added work per step is one Möbius addition/subtraction over the batch (O(B·d)), one 4096×256 by 256×512 affinity matmul (~0.54 GFLOP, sub-millisecond), and doubled distance matrices at levels 2 and 3. Measured estimate: +10–15% of the quantizer stage, i.e. 0.165–0.18 s per epoch, ~4.0–4.3 s per 24-step epoch pass total; 3000 epochs ≈ 8.5–9.0 minutes against the baseline's ~7.5–8.0 minutes. Extra trainable parameters: 2·512·d ≈ 65k at d = 64, negligible against the frozen budget. The 24556×256 behaviour-profile table is a fixed 25 MB buffer, not a parameter. Stage 3 protocol, sequence length and vocabulary usage are untouched apart from K2 = K3 = 512.
HYPOTHESIS: If the third token is being wasted because the flat-approximated residual collapses, then (a) the gyro residual keeps ‖r^3‖ at a curvature-determined scale instead of near zero, and (b) the affinity term splits each L2 cell's ~20 items into behaviourally coherent sub-groups, so the L3 code becomes a behaviour discriminator that Stage 3 can predict from the prefix and context. Worth keeping only if distinct L3 triples rise from 1298 to at least 3000, mean L3 codes per L2 cell rises from 1.04 to at least 2.5, mean affinity a_{i,k*} of assigned items exceeds 0.3, and d_P reconstruction stays within 5% of the baseline value while test_recall@10 exceeds 0.065.
RISKS: ['The affinity term pulls codes away from reconstruction-optimal choices and can trade semantic fidelity for partition (this is why the 5% reconstruction guard is recorded). 512 codes at level 2 may shatter the L1 hierarchy into noise. Möbius subtraction of two nearly aligned points at large radius can inflate ‖r‖ toward the boundary and route many items onto a few extreme codes, re-creating collapse in a different form. The 256-bin successor profile (≈96 items per bin) is smooth, so a_ik may be too weak to flip many argmins; if purity stays near zero the affinity is inert. A finer third token is harder for Stage 3 to generate, so prefix counts can rise while test_recall@10 falls — that is the outcome to record, not to hide.']
END IDEA

IDEA: BCMID-L3-RQ
TITLE: Successor-contrast Lorentz geodesic midpoint address with a 512-code curved L3 assignment
MOTIVATION: Round two moved every item toward a popularity-adjusted behaviour hub; prefix capacity fell to 230/1251/1298 and test_recall@10 fell to 0.0517. Round one kept 2201 L3 prefixes and reached 0.0544. The one consistent signal across both negatives is that recall tracks deep-prefix capacity. In the frozen 3-level 256-code quantizer there are 1769 distinct L2 pairs but only 2201 distinct L3 triples at 24556 items, i.e. 1.24 L3 codes per L2 pair: the third token is almost a deterministic function of the second, so the ~13.9 items sharing each L2 pair are behaviourally indistinguishable to the recommender. The deepest level is the cheapest place to buy behaviour-resolvable capacity, and no earlier round put behaviour there without also moving the points.
NOVELTY: (i) Geometry acts on the ADDRESS used for the code decision and on the decision boundary, never on the item positions: r_i is untouched, so the mechanism cannot merge cells by displacement as round two did. (ii) The behaviour object is a CENTRED successor-contrast direction (train transition row minus the global successor marginal, then SVD-truncated and L2-normalised), which structurally deletes the popularity/hub component that destroyed round two; contrast, not co-consumption mass. (iii) The curved operations are an exact Lorentz geodesic midpoint and the Klein power diagram (hyperbolic Voronoi), not a Frechet codebook update, not Sinkhorn, not a curvature-per-level controller, not successor-profile smoothing, not a cone, not a radial rank. (iv) L3 codewords go 256 -> 512, but the extra 256 codes are only usable because behaviour supplies a direction; capacity alone would just duplicate near-identical residuals.
CHANGE: At RQ level 3 only, the code index is chosen for a geodesic midpoint of the content residual point and a per-item behaviour point in the unit Poincare ball, against 512 codewords, by exact hyperbolic nearest-codeword; the RQ-VAE loss is unchanged, so the encoder is reshaped through the ordinary straight-through/commitment path and the token itself carries the behaviour.
SPECIFICATION: {'text': 'c = 1 (curvature -1, fixed); d = frozen RQ-VAE latent width.\nOFFLINE (train split, once): A_ij = adjacent (i->j) counts over train sequences; T_i = A_i/max(1,sum_j A_ij); pi = (sum_i A_i)/sum_ij A_ij; A~_i = T_i - pi; SVD A~ = U S V^T, keep m = smallest rank with cumulative squared singular energy >= 0.90 (reported), S_i = U_i S; S^_i = S_i/||S_i|| (0 if ||S_i|| < 1e-8). Fixed P in R^{d x m}, seed 0, N(0,1)/sqrt(m); h_i = P S^_i; R_b = median_i ||h_i||. Cache b_i = tanh(||h_i||/(2 R_b)) * h^_i for all 24556 train items (fixed buffer, no gradient).\nAPERTURE (once, after encoder init, train items only): R = median_i ||r_i^(3)||, r_i^(3) = z_i - e_{k1} - e_{k2}.\nPER STEP, batch B: x_i = exp_0^1(r_i^(3)/R) = tanh(||r_i||/(2R)) r^_i with ||r_i||/R clamped to 3.0; a_i = Mid_L(x_i, b_i); q_k = exp_0^1(e_k/R), k = 1..512 at L3 only (L1, L2 stay 256); K(a) = 2a/(1+||a||^2); gamma_k = (1-||K(q_k)||^2)^(-1/2); k_i = argmax_k gamma_k (<K(a_i),K(q_k)> - 1); quantized L3 vector = e_{k_i} straight-through; loss unchanged.'}
COST: offline (transition counts, rank-90% SVD, behaviour cache) ~10 s once. Per step at 1024 items/card: score matmul 1024x512x64 = 33.5M MAC (~0.07 GFLOP) plus ~1.3 MFLOP for exp/log/Klein/midpoint, i.e. <1% of a 6.0-6.7 ms step; per epoch 0.150 -> ~0.151 s, 3000 epochs ~450 -> ~452 s on four cards. Extra memory: 24556x64 behaviour cache (~6 MB) and 256x64 extra codewords. Stage3 adds 256 output-embedding rows at position 3 only.
HYPOTHESIS: The behaviour-resolved L3 address makes the third token informative, so distinct L3 prefixes rise well above 2201 (target >= 4000, mean L3 codes per L2 pair >= 2) with all 512 L3 codes occupied, within-prefix train successor entropy falls, and Stage3 test_recall@10 exceeds 0.065 while recall@5 and ndcg@10 rise with it. It is worth keeping if the rise in distinct triples and the behaviour-induced L3 flip fraction coexist with the recall gain; if triples do not rise, the mechanism is falsified by its own observable.
RISKS: ['The Lorentz midpoint contracts radii, which can push addresses toward the centre where curvature is weak and make geometry-off and both-on nearly identical (median address radius must be reported). The commitment/codebook terms may drag e_k back onto r_i and erase behaviour control at equilibrium (measured by the flip fraction). A 512-token level-3 vocabulary may be harder for Stage3 to learn. Centring does not fully remove blockbusters from the contrast signature. Klein cells are unbalanced, so some of the 512 codes may own almost no items. L3 reconstruction error will rise slightly.']
END IDEA

IDEA: CGREP-4L-RQ
TITLE: Contrast-weighted geodesic repulsion on quantised codewords with a fourth RQ level
MOTIVATION: Both negative rounds lost recall by MERGING deep prefixes (round two kept 1298 L3 prefixes at 0.05165, round one kept 2201 at 0.05439). The behaviour signal has so far only been used as an attractive force (move points toward a successor hub), which is exactly the operation that destroys depth. Separately, text-nearest items that are behaviourally unrelated keep sharing a prefix, and the 3x256 quantiser has no room left at level three. This idea reverses the sign of the behaviour force and adds the one architectural change the brief declares legal (a fourth level), so the partition can only become finer at depth.
NOVELTY: Not attraction to a popularity-adjusted successor barycentre (round two), not successor-weighted Frechet codebook updates, not per-level curvature control from prefix-transition scores, not radial position from context entropy, not Gromov-delta or ancestor-depth weighting, not a standalone hyperbolic auxiliary loss. It is the only repulsive, hinge-bounded, margin-terminated operator here, it acts on the QUANTISED code vectors rather than on the input points (so it can split a cluster but not create one), and it is paired with extra deep capacity instead of being asked to fit into the saturated three-level codebook.
CHANGE: Take the behaviourally most-contrasting text-nearest neighbours of each item inside the same level-2 prefix and push their quantised code vectors apart along the Poincare metric, with a hinge that switches off as soon as the pair is separated by the median initial geodesic distance; simultaneously widen the SID to four levels of 256 codewords so the newly created separation can be committed to tokens.
SPECIFICATION: {'text': 'For each item i, q_i = exp_0^c( sum_{l=1..4} e_{l,k_l(i)} ). Static precompute: p_i = add-one-smoothed directed training-transition distribution; contrast c_ij = 1 - cos(p_i,p_j); impostor set P = for each i the 4 text-kNN neighbours (frozen text embedding) with the largest c_ij. Margin m = median over P of d_P at initialisation. Loss L = L_RQVAE + lambda * mean_{(i,j) in batch, pi2(i)=pi2(j)} c_ij * [m - d_P(q_i,q_j)]_+^2, with STE so grad reaches e_{l,k_l(i)}; lambda = L_quant^(0)/L_push^(0) measured at step 0.'}
COST: +8192 parameters (one extra 256 x 32 codebook). Per step: at most 4096 x 4 = 16384 Poincare distance evaluations, roughly 0.1-0.4 ms on top of the ~6.3 ms step (24 steps/epoch, 0.15 s/epoch), so about +3-8 percent, i.e. 0.155-0.17 s/epoch and still ~8 minutes for 3000 epochs plus one ~1 minute GPU precompute of the impostor lists. Stage 3 pays one extra token per item.
HYPOTHESIS: If separation created by behaviour contrast is what the recall metric was reading (behaviour-contrast rho = +0.7104 in the 107-pair table) and prefix capacity was the binding constraint, then distinct L3 prefixes must rise above the 1298/2201 range, L4 must not collapse to a handful of codes, and Stage3 test_recall@10 must exceed 0.065. Observed through: distinct prefix counts per level, mean Poincare radius, L4 codebook perplexity, and test_recall@10 from the single frozen run.
RISKS: ["The outward drift can over-separate and starve the deep codebooks (all items far from every codeword) - the hinge margin limits this but L4 perplexity is the failure meter. The push can destroy text semantics that Stage 3 relies on for cold prefixes, in which case recall falls while prefix counts look healthy. A fourth token lengthens every Stage 3 sequence and may interact badly with the frozen protocol's context. Behaviour-contrast is measured only for items with outgoing transitions, so sparse items contribute nothing and the effect may be unevenly distributed. Seed noise is unmeasured because there is one run."]
END IDEA

IDEA: HOLO-TILT-L3
TITLE: Behaviour-contrast holonomy tilt of the deepest residual codebook in a Lorentz RQ-VAE
MOTIVATION: Both negative rounds moved item points toward a behaviour hub, which is algebraically a linear tilt of the assignment target and provably merges prefixes (L3 2201 -> 1298 cost 0.0027 recall). The frozen baseline (~0.0679) keeps a fine deep partition. What is missing is resolution in the direction the behaviour signal actually lives: the deepest level must be re-angled toward each item's successor-contrast direction, because the round-three diagnostics show the radial direction is group compactness, not hierarchy.
NOVELTY: An ISOMETRY OF THE TANGENT FRAME instead of a movement of points. No radial objective (so the round-one origin collapse is structurally absent), no successor Fréchet codebook, no per-level curvature control, no radial behaviour ranking, no branching MoE. The curved object is the holonomy (geodesic-triangle area) of the Lorentz model used as a rotation angle; the behaviour object is the per-item successor-contrast direction used only as a rotation plane. Capacity is added exactly where the evidence says it was lost: levels 2 and 3 go from 256 to 512 codewords, with the 3-token SID length and the frozen Stage-3 protocol untouched.
CHANGE: At level 3 only, each item's residual tangent vector is rotated by an angle equal to the hyperbolic area of the triangle (origin, prefix point, unit contrast probe), inside the plane spanned by the radial direction and that item's successor-contrast direction; the rotated query is matched against the ordinary residual codebook, which stays in one canonical frame.
SPECIFICATION: {'text': 'c gauge-fixed to 1. Levels [256,512,512]. Levels 1-2 and all losses are the frozen recipe. Level 3: k* = argmax_k [ <Rot_i r_i, w_k>_p - ||w_k||_p^2/2 ], with r_i = log_p(x_i), w_k = log_p(e_k), p the level-2 prefix point; Rot_i is the SO(2) rotation of angle theta_i = pi/2 - alpha - beta in the orthonormal pair (rho, u_perp), alpha = atan(tanh(b)/sinh(a_i)), beta = atan(tanh(a_i)/sinh(b)), a_i = d_L(o,x_i), b = median_i d_L(o,x_i) measured once after epoch 1 and then frozen. The frame (theta_i, rho, u_perp) is detached from autograd.'}
COST: Precompute of u_i once (seconds). Per step one O(d) rotation plus one Gram-Schmidt per item: ~1e6 flops per step at 24 steps/epoch and 3000 epochs, under 1% of the measured 0.145-0.16 s/epoch; plus 2 x 256 x d codebook parameters (~16k floats). Estimated 0.15-0.155 s/epoch, inside the four-GPU budget.
HYPOTHESIS: If the deep fan is tilted toward successor-contrast, the extra 512-codeword level-3 capacity acts as discriminative tokens, distinct L3 prefixes exceed the round-one 2201 and Stage-3 test_recall@10 exceeds 0.065; if the tilt is only assignment noise, prefixes stay flat and recall falls below the frozen baseline.
RISKS: ['The reconstruction objective can shrink the level-3 residual until the tilt is inert. Behaviour is item-specific while the codebook is shared, so the codebook cannot rotate for all items and reconstruction loss rises. theta reaching ~45-50 degrees at depth can turn the deepest token into an unusable extra bit. Items with no outgoing transitions get no tilt, splitting the population. Stage 3 may find a behaviour-tilted L3 harder to generate than a reconstruction residual.']
END IDEA

IDEA: BISECT-L4-ASYM
TITLE: Directed-transition asymmetry carved into a per-cell 4-symbol fourth SID digit by hyperbolic quantile bisection
MOTIVATION: The frozen chain is depth-starved: 24556 items share only 2201 distinct level-3 triples (about 1.24 level-3 codes per level-2 cell), so the deepest frozen level is nearly redundant, and every mechanism tried so far reduced that count further (1298 in round two) and lost recall. Behaviour information that separates items by how they are consumed predicts recall, but round two injected it by displacing item points toward a behaviour hub, which merged prefixes. The problem: put behaviour into the deepest tokens while increasing, not decreasing, the number of distinct deep cells.
NOVELTY: No global codebook is re-weighted, no input point is moved, no successor barycentre, no entropy/radial ranking, no per-level curvature scalar. A hierarchical product digit is attached per level-3 cell: each cell owns four child prototypes that are hyperbolic Fréchet centroids of the cell's directed-transition ASYMMETRY quantiles (forward-successor distribution versus backward-predecessor distribution), and the child is chosen by a two-anchor weighted Poincaré score whose second term is scaled by the item's own asymmetry. None of per-cell shared-alphabet refinement, forward/backward asymmetry, or a two-anchor weighted Poincaré assignment exists in the repository, and the two-term sum is precisely what keeps the curvature from being a pure gauge.
CHANGE: Add a fourth SID token from a shared alphabet {0,1,2,3}, keyed by (l1,l2,l3,child); child vectors are trainable but born at frozen hyperbolic asymmetry-quantile centroids, and each assignment is the argmin over j of d_c(xi,u_kj) + b_i·d_c(xi,v_kj).
SPECIFICATION: {'text': "Offline on the training split, build the first-order transition count matrix F and the per-item support-shrunk forward/backward Jensen-Shannon asymmetry b_i in [0,1]. Fix c = (1/(1.2R))^2 from the measured initial latent radius R. At the end of epoch 1, cut every level-3 cell's items into four equal-mass b-quantiles, compute each quantile's hyperbolic Fréchet centroid v_kj, and clone it into a trainable u_kj. Every step the frozen levels 1-3 run unchanged; level 4 is the argmin of the two-anchor score; the quantized latent is q1+q2+q3+u_k[l4] with a straight-through residual; the baseline reconstruction and commitment losses now include level 4."}
COST: +1024 trainable and +1024 frozen child vectors (d=64: about 131k parameters, under 1% of the encoder); per step 4096 items x 4 children x 2 anchors = 32768 Poincaré distances at d=64 (about 4M FLOP, under 3% of an encoder step) plus 4096 four-way argmins. At the frozen scale (24 steps/epoch, 3000 epochs, 0.145-0.16 s/epoch) the projected overhead is at most +0.004 s/epoch, i.e. at most +12 s over the whole Stage-2 run; the one-off quantile/centroid pass is O(N log N) over 24556 items and costs seconds.
HYPOTHESIS: Worth keeping only if the fourth digit actually spreads items, i.e. distinct four-token SIDs rise from about 2201 to at least 6000 with no level-3 cell collapsing onto a single child, and child index tracks the asymmetry quantile the child was born from. If both hold, Stage 3 sees a finer, behaviour-labelled deep partition without any input displacement and test_recall@10 should exceed 0.065. If the digit collapses (all items of a cell to one child) the mechanism is a no-op and the merge lesson predicts no gain.
RISKS: ['(1) A fourth token lengthens Stage-3 generation by one step and may cost precision even with a finer SID. (2) Transition asymmetry may be sparse: items with fewer than 5 transitions fall back to the smoothed default and their children degrade toward text quartiles, so behaviour stops reaching the tokens. (3) Freezing v at the end of epoch 1 may lock a bad geometry if the encoder drifts; an EMA would introduce a non-derivable constant, so it is deliberately not used. (4) Curvature is a gauge, so any measured gain must come from the two-anchor sum and the per-cell prototypes, not from the value of c. (5) Child usage imbalance could make the 4-symbol alphabet effectively binary.']
END IDEA

IDEA: HYSPLIT-BEHV-RQ
TITLE: Behaviour-contrast hyperbolic dyadic refinement of the deepest RQ codebook
MOTIVATION: The two negative rounds both lost recall exactly when deep prefix capacity fell (2201 distinct L3 prefixes → 0.0544; 1298 → 0.0517), and both lost capacity by moving input points toward a behaviour hub. The behaviour signal that does predict recall on the 107 confirmed pairs is behaviour-CONTRAST, not Gromov-delta, not ancestor depth. So the useful place for behaviour is not the item position (it merges) but the DEEP CODEBOOK: let the deepest level be doubled into behaviour-polarized child codewords whose offsets are measured from the training transition contrast, so the level-3 partition becomes strictly finer and the extra tokens carry behaviour rather than duplicating it.
NOVELTY: Round one/two moved items and residuals (merging). The rejected ideas ranked items radially (BRad-RQ), set curvature from a prefix-transition score (CURVCTRL-SID), used successor-weighted Fréchet codebook means (poincare-frechet-successor-codebook), or built cones/tree-embeddings. None of them *generated extra codewords* from a behaviour statistic. Here no point moves; the codebook itself is refined by a measured behaviour contrast through the Poincaré exponential map, doubling deep-level capacity at zero free parameters (the offsets are buffers, not trained), so it cannot collapse to the origin and cannot over-merge.
CHANGE: Replace the deepest level's K-codeword nearest-neighbour by a 2K structured codebook: each anchor codeword c_k spawns two children exp_{c_k}(±rho_k u_k), where u_k is the EMA of the mean behaviour-contrast vector of the items currently assigned to anchor k and rho_k is the EMA of the median absolute tangent projection of those items on u_k.
